interactions.label: A haemoglobin of 10.8 g/dL in the second trimester of pregnancy can be a physiol

params.question: A haemoglobin of 10.8 g/dL in the second trimester of pregnancy can be a physiological finding and does not always indicate anaemia.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is actually true. The disproportionate rise in plasma volume compared to red cell mass creates physiological haemodilution. A haemoglobin of 10.8 g/dL in the second trimester is above the WHO anaemia threshold of 10.5 g/dL and can be entirely physiological.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Plasma volume rises by 40–50% while red cell mass increases by only 20–30%, diluting the blood. The WHO threshold for anaemia in the second trimester is below 10.5 g/dL, so 10.8 g/dL falls within the physiological range created by haemodilution.

interactions.label: A gravida 2 at her booking visit reports her last menstrual period as 10 weeks a

params.question: A gravida 2 at her booking visit reports her last menstrual period as 10 weeks ago, but a dating ultrasound estimates the gestational age at 14 weeks. If the LMP-based date is accepted uncorrected, which clinical decision is most likely to be adversely affected?

answers.text: Selection of appropriate iron supplementation dosage

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Iron supplementation is recommended throughout pregnancy and is not critically dependent on exact gestational age. The real danger of a 4-week dating error lies in timing-critical decisions such as preterm labour management.

answers.text: Scheduling of the oral glucose tolerance test

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: While the OGTT is typically scheduled at 24–28 weeks, a 4-week shift in its timing is unlikely to cause as serious a management error as miscalculating the threshold for corticosteroid administration.

answers.text: Timing of the first dose of tetanus toxoid immunisation

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Tetanus toxoid follows a fixed schedule relative to the pregnancy and is not as critically gestational-age-dependent as decisions about preterm labour and corticosteroid administration.

answers.text: Administration of antenatal corticosteroids if she presents with preterm contractions

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Corticosteroids are indicated between 24–34 weeks for threatened preterm birth. A 4-week dating error could mean the woman is actually 34 weeks when the team believes she is only 30 — fundamentally changing whether steroids are indicated and how labour is managed.

overallFeedback.feedback: The key principle is that gestational age, primarily derived from the LMP and confirmed by ultrasound, drives timing-critical decisions. Corticosteroid administration (24–34 weeks) is among the most consequential — a 4-week error could place the woman beyond the treatment window without the team realising it.

Exactly right. Gestational age derived from the LMP is the reference point for nearly every obstetric decision. Corticosteroid timing is one of the most consequential decisions that depends on accurate dating.

interactions.label: A couple planning their first pregnancy asks about preventing neural tube defect

params.question: A couple planning their first pregnancy asks about preventing neural tube defects. When should folic acid supplementation ideally be started?

answers.text: At the time of the first missed menstrual period

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: By the time of the first missed period, the embryo is already 4–5 weeks post-conception and neural tube closure is complete or nearly so. Folic acid stores must be adequate before conception to be protective.

answers.text: During the second trimester when fetal growth is most rapid

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Neural tube closure occurs within the first 28 days after conception, well within the first trimester. Second-trimester supplementation cannot prevent neural tube defects.

answers.text: At least three months before planned conception

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Neural tube closure occurs within the first 28 days after conception — often before the woman knows she is pregnant. Starting folic acid at least three months beforehand ensures adequate tissue stores are in place when the critical window arrives.

answers.text: At the first antenatal visit after pregnancy is confirmed

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The first antenatal visit typically occurs at 6–8 weeks or later, by which time neural tube closure is already complete. Prevention requires pre-conception supplementation.

overallFeedback.feedback: The critical window for neural tube closure is the first 28 days after conception — before most women know they are pregnant. For folic acid to be protective, it must be started at least three months before conception so that tissue stores are adequate when organogenesis begins.
Well done. Pre-conception folic acid supplementation is one of the most effective preventive interventions in obstetrics, reducing neural tube defect risk by up to 70%.

params.question: At a primary health centre without neonatal intensive care facilities, a biophysical profile score of 4 out of 10 is obtained at 36 weeks in a growth-restricted fetus. What is the most appropriate next step?

answers.text: Reassure the mother and repeat the biophysical profile in one week

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: A BPP of 4/10 indicates significant fetal compromise. In the context of growth restriction at 36 weeks, waiting a week risks fetal death. This score warrants urgent action, not watchful waiting.

answers.text: Arrange urgent transfer to a tertiary centre with NICU facilities

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The BPP score warrants delivery planning, but the facility lacks neonatal intensive care. The safest course is urgent transfer to a tertiary centre equipped for both operative delivery and neonatal resuscitation, balancing urgency against transport risk.

answers.text: Administer corticosteroids and wait 48 hours for lung maturity

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: At 36 weeks, fetal lungs are usually sufficiently mature, and the standard corticosteroid window (up to 34 weeks) has passed. Delaying delivery for 48 hours with a BPP of 4/10 in growth restriction is hazardous.

answers.text: Perform an immediate caesarean delivery at the primary health centre

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: While the BPP indicates urgency, performing a caesarean at a facility without NICU capability puts the already compromised neonate at extreme risk. The appropriate response is transfer to a suitably equipped centre.

overallFeedback.feedback: Interpreting surveillance findings is never a binary exercise. A BPP of 4/10 at 36 weeks in growth restriction demands urgent action, but that action must be matched to the facility. Without NICU capability, urgent transfer to a tertiary centre is the safest response.

Correct. This question illustrates the principle that surveillance interpretation must integrate the test result, the clinical context, and the facility's capabilities — the most dangerous error is binary thinking that ignores what the facility can actually offer.

params.question: A woman at 34 weeks presents with absent fetal movements for six hours. Ultrasound confirms no fetal cardiac activity. The delivered fetus has intact skin and preserved body structure with no discolouration or skull bone overlap. What is the most important clinical implication of these findings?

answers.text: The stillbirth is classified as fresh, indicating death occurred recently and was potentially preventable with adequate intrapartum monitoring

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: A fresh stillbirth, characterised by intact skin and preserved body structure, indicates death within the preceding 24 hours — often during or just before labour. Fresh stillbirths are largely preventable with good intrapartum monitoring, making their review critical for quality improvement.

answers.text: The presence of intact skin rules out placental pathology as a possible cause of death

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Intact skin indicates recent death but does not exclude placental pathology. Acute placental abruption and cord complications can cause rapid fetal death with fresh stillbirth findings.

answers.text: Spalding's sign will develop within hours, confirming a macerated stillbirth

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Spalding's sign — overlapping skull bones — is a feature of maceration that develops days after fetal death in utero, not within hours. Intact skin and preserved structure indicate a fresh, not macerated, stillbirth.

answers.text: The absence of maceration means the stillbirth does not require further investigation

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: All stillbirths warrant thorough investigation regardless of maceration status. Fresh stillbirths especially merit detailed review because their recency suggests they may have been preventable with timely intervention.

overallFeedback.feedback: The key distinction is between fresh and macerated stillbirth. Intact skin and preserved body structure indicate a fresh stillbirth — death within the past 24 hours. This matters because fresh stillbirths are largely preventable with adequate monitoring, making their analysis critical for preventing future deaths.
Correct. Distinguishing fresh from macerated stillbirth has direct clinical significance — fresh stillbirths point to potentially preventable intrapartum events and drive quality-of-care review.

interactions.label: Priya, a 22-year-old primigravida, presents at 32 weeks with severe pre-eclampsi

params.question: Priya, a 22-year-old primigravida, presents at 32 weeks with severe pre-eclampsia (BP 158/104, 2+ proteinuria) and severe anaemia (Hb 7.2 g/dL), having had no antenatal care since a urine pregnancy test in the first trimester. Which statement best captures the fundamental failure in her care?

answers.text: The primary health centre lacked ultrasound equipment for early diagnosis of her conditions

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The conditions that escalated — hypertension and anaemia — are detected by blood pressure measurement and haemoglobin testing, not ultrasound. The failure was in the absence of any structured follow-up, not in equipment availability.

answers.text: Pre-eclampsia and severe anaemia are inherently unpredictable and cannot be detected through routine antenatal screening

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Both conditions develop gradually. Blood pressure rises progressively and haemoglobin falls over weeks. Structured ANC with regular checks at defined intervals is specifically designed to catch these trajectories before they reach crisis.

answers.text: Young maternal age placed Priya in a low-risk category where frequent antenatal visits were considered unnecessary

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Age alone does not determine the need for antenatal surveillance. All pregnant women require structured periodic monitoring because risk status is dynamic — a woman low-risk at booking can develop complications at any point.

answers.text: The absence of structured, periodic antenatal surveillance eliminated every opportunity to detect gradually worsening blood pressure and haemoglobin before crisis

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Structured ANC builds in regular blood pressure, urine, and haemoglobin checks at defined intervals. Both pre-eclampsia and anaemia develop gradually and would have been flagged weeks before reaching crisis. The fundamental failure was the absence of the surveillance system itself.

overallFeedback.feedback: The central lesson of Priya's case is that both pre-eclampsia and anaemia develop gradually and are detectable at routine ANC contacts. The failure was not in diagnosis or equipment — it was in the complete absence of the structured surveillance system that defines antenatal care.

Well reasoned. Priya's case demonstrates that antenatal care is not optional — it is a structured surveillance system where every visit is an opportunity to detect developing complications before they become emergencies.
